answer.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure creates urgency, but memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention—directly opposing the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. A discounting race is a losing strategy. Instead, deploy proven levers that improve perceived value without eroding margins or retention. Memory_91 (in-product activation messaging) drove week-one engagement +11%, activation +6%, and retained 30-day retention +1%. This directly addresses SMB churn risk by accelerating time-to-value and demonstrating product value—reducing price sensitivity. Memory_86 confirms simplified onboarding is also effective, but activation messaging has fresher signal and targets engagement directly. A standard_experiment roll-out tests this at realistic scale without overcommitting. This preserves optionality: if activation messaging stabilizes churn, we've won without margin damage; if it underperforms, we retain budget for enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) or referral_incentive (memory_57) in follow-up cycles. Avoids the known retention trap while buying time for better long-term competitive positioning.
